title: The 4 Patterns of AI Native Development — Patrick Debois
talk_summary: Patrick Debois frames AI-native development as four role shifts for developers: from producer to manager of agents, from implementation to specifying intent, from delivery to discovery, and from output to captured knowledge.

takeaways.technique: Summary-first review instead of raw diff
takeaways.what_they_do: Strip the generated change down to a compact summary the reviewer can accept/reject at a glance, rather than reading a red/green diff or verbose chat log.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the review kind of strips whatever we need um to review the code uh into uh almost like a summary and then we kind of say yes no

takeaways.technique: Non-text review artifacts (diagrams) for change impact
takeaways.what_they_do: Render what changed as a diagram instead of text so impact and errors are easier to spot.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is an example of creating a diagram of what has changed a lot easier to review

takeaways.technique: Explicit guardrails and file locks for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Manager-style constraints: agents may not touch certain files, files can be locked, and agent permissions are scoped.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do want to set constraints like AI you cannot touch this much like a manager sets the rules

takeaways.technique: Per-run cost and duration tracking for long agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat long-running agent sessions as the unit of cost, watching duration and dollars per run, not per prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It is not just about that one prompt. Uh it is about like that long running prompt. So how long did it take? Well, in this case almost $10.

takeaways.what_they_do: Save intermediate state so a long agent run can be resumed or regenerated from a checkpoint instead of redoing the whole train of thought.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's been checkpoints because we don't want to generate the whole kind of like train of thought

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep a durable record of features tried, dismissed, and why, so the same idea isn't re-litigated and decisions aren't lost in tickets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe we can keep actually track of whatever feature in almost like a feature memory. And we're not doing this over over again.
